text:
maria: pushed fixups for the scheduler test flake and squashed commits. addressed @alex and @ben's comments — re-requesting review when you have a moment. CI is currently showing one failing integration job (link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/482).

alex: thanks, i'll take a look. can you paste the failing test output?

maria: sure — failing snippet:
```text
E   TimeoutError: 5 seconds exceeded while waiting for queue drain
  File "tests/scheduler/test_lane.py", line 42, in test_queue_drain
```
I tweaked the test to wait on the event with a 10s fallback and bumped a small sleep in the fixture. local run passes: `pytest tests/scheduler -q`.

ben: LGTM for the test change. small nit on naming: `_wait_for_drain` -> `wait_for_drain_timeout`? not blocking though. @alex PTAL. :+1:

ci-bot: build #8421: integration-tests failed — error in test_scheduler/queue_drain. Rerun? :arrows_counterclockwise:

alex: i'll run the integration job locally and kick a CI rerun on GH. if it's still flaky we can temporarily mark it with @flaky and follow up with an infra ticket.

maria: thanks. i ran the integration suite on my dev VM (amd64) and got green. command i used:
```bash
pytest tests/integration/test_scheduler.py::test_queue_drain -q -k queue_drain
```
If CI keeps failing i'm fine marking it flaky for this release and opening an infra follow-up.

jess: pinging for the canary cut — we have a canary at 16:00 PT. do we need to hold?

alex: if CI clears by 15:30 PT we can include it in the canary, otherwise defer to the next one.

maria: OK will monitor and update in here. re-requesting review: @alex @ben
